userStories.title: Job panel transcript entry and layout
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Render the job view as a collapsible transcript card with progress, stories, advisor decisions and log rows.

**Motivation** — The chat shows nothing until the `[nax-jobs] ... ended` notice, often hours later.

**Approach** — Add `| { kind: "job"; view: JobPanelView; open?: boolean }` to TranscriptEntry, add layout-job.ts and the layout.ts dispatch case, and extend ChatGlyphs with progressFull (`"█"`, ASCII `"#"`) and progressEmpty (`"░"`, ASCII `"."`).

Panel layout: Collapsed (default), two rows for a `run`/`finish` job with progress, one row otherwise; the explicit row-2 condition below also includes decision-only panels.

- Row 1: the theme's `pointer` glyph, `nax <kind> <target>` (bot kinds: `nax bot review #<target>` / `nax bot fix #<target>`), the state word, `formatElapsed(elapsedMs)`, and `$<cost to 2 decimals>` when `cost` is set, separated by two spaces. The state word is coloured: `running` accent, `succeeded` success, `failed` and `lost` danger, `cancelled` warning. Row 1 ends with the theme's show/hide hint.
- Row 2 is drawn when `progress` is set or there is at least one decision; without `progress` it starts at the decisions part. Row 2: `JOB_PROGRESS_CELLS` cells, `round(JOB_PROGRESS_CELLS * passed / total)` of them `progressFull` (accent) and the rest `progressEmpty` (muted), then `<passed>/<total>`; then ` · <storyId> <phase>` when `current` is set; then ` · <n> advisor decision` for one or ` · <n> advisor decisions` for more (without the leading ` · ` when nothing precedes it), with ` (<m> flagged)` in the warning colour when `m > 0`. A `total` of 0 draws all cells empty.
- `formatElapsed`: under 60 s `<s>s`; under 60 min `<m>m`; otherwise `<h>h <mm>m` with two-digit minutes.

Expanded adds, after the collapsed rows, three sections in this order, each under a muted heading row and indented with `cardIndent`: `stories` (one row per story: a status word — `passed` success, `failed`/`regression-failed` danger, `in-progress` accent, everything else muted — then `<id> <title>`, and `◂ <phase>` after the current story), `advisor decisions` (one row per decision line, at most `JOB_PANEL_DECISION_ROWS` (10) rows followed by `+<n> more` when there are more; a flagged row starts with the theme's `warning` glyph and is drawn in the warning colour), and `log` (the log tail rows, muted). A section with nothing to show is omitted. Rows wrap to the transcript width through `cardRows`. With colour off every row is the same text without colour.

The progress algorithm, not the illustrative diagram, governs: { passed: 4, total: 13 } gives 5 full and 11 empty cells. The first row's pointer is followed by one space before nax; the command/state/elapsed/cost fields have the specified two-space gaps and the hint a single-space separator. Value imports across modules go through barrels (`check:alias-internals`); the TUI imports chat values/types from @/chat.

**Scope** — In: new job entry union member, pure layout-job renderer, dispatcher and theme glyphs. Out: US-001 source gathering/projection; US-003 polling, upsert, click toggles and cachedLines own-expansion wiring; US-004 clock rows; US-005–US-007 compaction. Any change to the footer job strip or a footer idle-time readout; `chat-status.ts` stays as it is. A row cap for the `stories` section (a PRD's story count is already bounded by the planner).

**Interface** — verbatim TypeScript:
```typescript
// packages/nax/src/tui/chat/layout-job.ts
export const JOB_PROGRESS_CELLS = 16;
export const JOB_PANEL_DECISION_ROWS = 10;
export function formatElapsed(ms: number): string;
export function jobPanelLines(entry: Extract<TranscriptEntry, { kind: "job" }>, context: LayoutContext): readonly StyledLine[];
```

Use layout-background.ts and layout-lines.ts for the existing card indentation, sanitization, hint and wrapping conventions. Write direct text/span tests with Unicode, ASCII, colour-off and narrow contexts before implementing the renderer.

userStories.title: Live job panels in the chat
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Subscribe chat transcripts to live job views without splitting streaming replies, losing expansion state or freezing stale terminal results.

**Motivation** — A job launched from chat runs headless (`chat/jobs/job-runner.ts`, output to `<outputDir>/chat-jobs/<id>.log`).

**Approach** — `useJobPanels({ host, setEntries, turnRunning })`:

- Does nothing when `host.jobs` is absent.
- Subscribes to `host.jobs.onChange`. On every change, and every `JOB_PANEL_REFRESH_MS` while at least one paneled job is `running`, it refreshes the paneled jobs.
- A job becomes paneled when it is `running` and is not yet paneled: a job started in this chat and a job re-attached when the chat opened both qualify. A job already ended when first seen is never paneled. The paneled set lives in the hook, so after `/clear` or a resume replaces the entries, the next refresh of a still-paneled job appends its panel again.
- The hook keeps two per-job sets: `paneled` (jobs it shows) and `appended` (jobs whose entry it has added since the entries were last replaced). While `turnRunning` is true a refresh of a job not in `appended` computes its view but does not call `setEntries` (a turn's reply is still streaming, and an entry appended after it would split the reply); refreshes of `appended` jobs replace their entry in place. On the `turnRunning` true-to-false edge the hook runs one refresh for every `paneled` job not in `appended`, including a job that ended during the turn, so its panel appears after the turn showing its final state.
- The decision is made against the current entries inside the `setEntries` updater with `hasJobPanel`, so after the entries are replaced (`/clear`, resume) a job with no entry is again a first append and follows the same `turnRunning` rule; `appended` only drives the true-to-false flush.
- A refresh calls `readJobPanelView` for the job and applies `setEntries((rows) => upsertJobPanel(rows, view))`.
- Refreshes are serialized per job: a refresh for a job does not start while an earlier one for that job is pending. A job that has ended gets exactly one more applied refresh, started after any pending one settles (and, for a job not yet appended, held until the turn ends), so its result is the last one applied and the panel freezes on the final state. The job is not refreshed after that.
- On unmount it unsubscribes and clears its timer.

`upsertJobPanel(entries, view)` replaces the `job` entry whose `view.jobId` matches, keeping its `open` flag and its position; with no match it appends `{ kind: "job", view }`. It returns a new array and never mutates its input. `hasJobPanel(entries, jobId)` says whether a `job` entry for that id exists; inside the `setEntries` updater the hook uses it to decide, per the rule above, between replacing and holding back an append while a turn runs.

`ChatApp.tsx` calls `useJobPanels({ host, setEntries, turnRunning })` once. The `[nax-jobs]` notice to the agent, the background notice entry and the footer job strip are unchanged.

`CollapsibleEntry` includes `"job"`, and a `job` entry toggles on its first row only, as a `background` entry does. In `cachedLines`, `job` joins the list using `entry.open ?? base.expanded`, so a panel's own `open` flag decides its expansion.

New code goes in new files. `packages/nax/src/tui/chat/chat-status.ts` is at the 600-line source limit and must not grow; `ChatApp.tsx` gains only the hook calls. `setInterval` is banned; timers use `setTimeout` with `clearTimeout`, the documented exception for a timer cancelled mid-flight. Each such call site carries the one-line comment saying so. Value imports across modules go through barrels (`check:alias-internals`); consume readJobPanelView from @/chat. The panel and the idle compactor are display and host behaviour only: none of the panel's content is added to the agent's context.

**Scope** — In: job-panel-entries.ts, use-job-panels.ts, first-row click behavior, cachedLines own expansion and one ChatApp hook call. Out: US-001 artifact reader changes; US-002 renderer/theme implementation; US-004 turn stats; US-005–US-007 compaction. A pending-ask section in the job panel; run asks keep reaching the chat as today's notices and cards. Any change to the footer job strip or a footer idle-time readout; `chat-status.ts` stays as it is. Adding the panel content to the agent's context. Making `JOB_PANEL_LOG_LINES`, `JOB_PANEL_REFRESH_MS` or `IDLE_COMPACT_MIN_TOKENS` configurable.

**Interface** — verbatim TypeScript:
```typescript
// packages/nax/src/tui/chat/job-panel-entries.ts
export function upsertJobPanel(entries: readonly TranscriptEntry[], view: JobPanelView): readonly TranscriptEntry[];
export function hasJobPanel(entries: readonly TranscriptEntry[], jobId: string): boolean;

// packages/nax/src/tui/chat/use-job-panels.ts
export const JOB_PANEL_REFRESH_MS = 2000;
export function useJobPanels(input: { readonly host: ChatHost; readonly setEntries: (update: (rows: readonly TranscriptEntry[]) => readonly TranscriptEntry[]) => void; readonly turnRunning: boolean }): void;
```

Seam: US-003 consumes readJobPanelView (US-001) and jobPanelLines via the job entry (US-002). Its seam ACs enter at the ChatJobs.onChange listener the hook subscribes and observe setEntries. Write integration tests with fake time and controllable pending reads, including terminal notification during a pending read and entry replacement during a running turn. Preserve unrelated entry identities, unsubscribe on unmount and prevent late async continuations from applying state after disposal.

[unit] upsertJobPanel with an existing job entry for run-1 replaces it at the same index.
[unit] upsertJobPanel keeps the replaced entry's open flag.

[integration] When host.jobs.onChange fires for a newly running job run-1 with turnRunning false, useJobPanels calls setEntries with an update that appends a job entry whose view.jobId is run-1.

[integration] When host.jobs.onChange fires for a newly running job with turnRunning true, useJobPanels leaves the entries without a job entry for it while turnRunning stays true, across refresh ticks.
[integration] When turnRunning changes from true to false, useJobPanels appends the panel of a job that became running during the turn.
[integration] A job that starts and ends while turnRunning is true gets a panel showing its ended state once turnRunning becomes false.

routing.reasoning: Per-job serialized refreshes, terminal races, deferred streaming-safe append, replaced entries and React timer/subscription cleanup require coordinated state-machine and UI integration tests.

suggestedCriteria: When a paneled entry is cleared during a running turn, useJobPanels does not reappend it until turnRunning becomes false.

When a paneled job's final view is applied, later onChange events do not read or replace its frozen panel.
When an already appended panel refreshes while a reply streams, the existing reply entry retains its position and uninterrupted text.
When the hook unmounts before a pending read resolves, resolving that read does not call setEntries.

userStories.title: Turn end time on the stats row
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Leave a muted local end-time row for every observed top-level chat turn_end, including zero-output and unsuccessful turns.

**Motivation** — It has no end time, so after a long run the user cannot tell how long the chat has been idle or whether the prompt cache has expired.

**Approach** — `turnEndClock(endedAt, now)` renders the local time of `endedAt` as `HH:MM` (24-hour, two digits each) when it falls on the same local calendar day as `now`, and as `<Mon> <D> HH:MM` (`Nov 14 23:05`, English three-letter month) otherwise. An `endedAt` that does not parse renders as the empty string.

`turnStatsText` with `endedAt` appends ` · <turnEndClock(endedAt, now)>` (nothing when the clock is empty); without `endedAt` its output is unchanged.

`turnStatsEntry(events, end, now)`:

1. `completed` with output tokens: today's row plus ` · <clock>`, e.g. `48.2 tok/s · 1.3k out · 14s · 14:32`.
2. `completed` with no output tokens: `0 out · <s>s · <clock>`.
3. `cancelled`, `timed_out`, `interrupted`, `errored`: `<status word> · <clock>`, where the words are `cancelled`, `timed out`, `interrupted`, `errored`. When the clock is empty (an unparseable `end.at`) the row is the status word alone. This row is drawn in addition to the existing `Interrupted by user` or error row, so every turn ends with its time.

The clock comes from `end.at`. Times are local, so tests build `end.at` from local date parts.

Target: `turnStatsEntry(events, end, now: Date = new Date()): TranscriptEntry`; always returns a row. `ChatApp.tsx` appends the row for every turn end. Preserve top-level/subagent exclusion and per-turn event isolation in the existing call site.

Update existing assertions, not just new tests: packages/nax/test/ui/chat/turn-stats.test.tsx's completed/no-rate/own-events rows currently assert clockless text, and cancelled/errored/zero-output cases assert no row. Replace them with the new clock-bearing invariants, using local date parts. The UI's stats-row observer must now see status-only rows as well as output-token rows. `AC-13 replays its history without any stats row` is unchanged. packages/nax/test/unit/tui/chat/turn-stats.test.ts likewise replaces completed/invalid-start clockless expectations and non-completed/zero-output undefined expectations. Keep invalid-start elapsed time at 0 while adding the end clock.

**Scope** — In: turnEndClock, optional formatter inputs, always-returned turnStatsEntry, minimal ChatApp append adjustment and updates to existing stats tests. Out: US-001–US-003 job panels; US-005–US-007 compaction. Turn end times for a resumed session's replayed history. A turn-end row for a send that rejects before any `turn_end` event. Any change to the footer job strip or a footer idle-time readout; `chat-status.ts` stays as it is.

**Interface** — verbatim TypeScript:
```typescript
// packages/nax/src/tui/chat/turn-stats.ts
export function turnEndClock(endedAt: string, now: Date): string;
```
Target formatter input: `turnStatsText(input: { rate; outputTokens; elapsedMs; endedAt?: string; now?: Date }): string`. Target row builder: `turnStatsEntry(events, end, now: Date = new Date()): TranscriptEntry`.

Use deterministic local-date fixtures and preserve the existing muted turn-stats renderer. Do not change decodeRate's window aggregation or synthesize event timestamps from rendering time.

userStories.title: Absolute token cap for native compaction
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Add an optional absolute native-session compaction trigger and a retention budget scaled to the trigger that actually wins.

**Motivation** — On a 1M-token window that is about 900k tokens, so the first turn after a multi-hour job pays a full cache write on a very large context.

**Approach** — `compactionThreshold(window, cfg)` and `keepBudget(window, cfg, aggressive)` apply, in this order:

1. `percentThreshold = min(floor(window * compactAtPercent / 100), window - headroom)` (today's rule).
2. When `cfg.compactAtTokens` is set and greater than 0, `threshold = min(percentThreshold, compactAtTokens)`; otherwise `threshold = percentThreshold`.
3. `keepBudget`: when step 2 lowered the threshold (the cap is below `percentThreshold`), `budget = floor(compactAtTokens * keepRecentPercent / compactAtPercent)`; otherwise today's `floor(window * keepRecentPercent / 100)`.
4. `aggressive` halves the step-3 budget, as today.

Because the schema requires `keepRecentPercent <= compactAtPercent - 20`, the step-3 budget is always below the threshold it pairs with, so a compaction can never leave history above its own trigger.

`ResolvedCompaction` — Target: gains `readonly compactAtTokens?: number`. `NativeBackendOptions.compaction` — Target: gains `readonly compactAtTokens?: number`.

`compactionSettingsSchema` — Target: gains `compactAtTokens: z.number().int().optional()` accepting 0 or a value of at least `MIN_COMPACT_AT_TOKENS` (10000), with the message `compactAtTokens must be 0 (off) or at least 10000`; `DEFAULT_COMPACTION` is unchanged. This is the shared schema, so `execution.compaction.compactAtTokens` becomes a valid setting for every native session that reads `execution.compaction` (story sessions, chat subagents, the `nax-agent` ACP server in `nax-agent-acp/src/server/main.ts`) with no default, meaning no cap. The chat session alone gets its cap from `chat.compaction` (below), which always replaces any `execution.compaction.compactAtTokens` for the chat.

The chat-specific override is US-006's responsibility. With `compactAtTokens` 0, use the percent rule only (today's behaviour). Preserve shouldCompact's enabled gate and strict above-threshold comparison. Keep DEFAULT_COMPACTION, resolveCompaction(undefined) and every existing uncapped threshold/budget assertion unchanged. Export MIN_COMPACT_AT_TOKENS from @nathapp/nax-agent/internal, using the existing explicit compaction-settings export; do not expose private seams from the public root. The existing nativeBackend resolveCompaction path must carry the optional field through without a second resolver.

**Scope** — In: ResolvedCompaction, shared compaction settings schema/constant/internal export, NativeBackendOptions.compaction and threshold/retention arithmetic within packages/nax-agent. Out: US-006 nax runtime types/chat defaults/chat option composition; US-007 idle timers/UI; US-001–US-004 display work. A reason on the automatic token-cap compaction's transcript row; only the idle compaction names its reason. No new ACP-owned context-compaction policy: existing execution.compaction consumers only gain the explicitly configured optional field.

**Interface** — verbatim TypeScript:

userStories.title: Chat compaction config and the native chat session cap
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Resolve chat-specific compaction defaults and override only the native chat session's absolute token cap while retaining execution settings for other sessions.

**Motivation** — The native chat compacts only at `execution.compaction.compactAtPercent` (default 90) of the model window.

**Approach** — This feature extends the `chat` config block (`ChatConfigSchema`) added by the `chat-workflow-flow` feature, so it runs after that feature is merged. In this worktree those prerequisite files are absent; extend them after the prerequisite merge, without implementing a competing chat-workflow configuration.

`chat.compaction` config:
```json
{ "chat": { "compaction": { "compactAtTokens": 200000, "idleCompactAfterMinutes": 55 } } }
```

`compactAtTokens` follows the shared rule, 0 or an integer of at least `MIN_COMPACT_AT_TOKENS` (10000), with the same message `compactAtTokens must be 0 (off) or at least 10000` (default `DEFAULT_CHAT_COMPACT_AT_TOKENS`); `MIN_COMPACT_AT_TOKENS` is exported from `@nathapp/nax-agent/internal` and the chat schema imports it there; `idleCompactAfterMinutes` is an integer from 0 to 1440 (default `DEFAULT_IDLE_COMPACT_AFTER_MINUTES`); 0 turns each off. With no `chat.compaction` block both defaults apply.

`chatCompactAtTokens(config)` is `config.chat?.compaction?.compactAtTokens ?? DEFAULT_CHAT_COMPACT_AT_TOKENS`; 0 turns the cap off. Only the native chat session (`open-chat-session.ts`) takes it; story sessions and chat subagents keep `execution.compaction` as configured.

Chat session options in `packages/nax/src/chat/open-chat-session.ts` — Target: `{ ...request.config.execution.compaction, compactAtTokens: chatCompactAtTokens(request.config) }`.

`ChatConfigSchema` in `packages/nax/src/config/schemas-chat.ts` and `ChatConfig` in `runtime-types-chat.ts` — Target: gain `compaction?: { compactAtTokens: number; idleCompactAfterMinutes: number }`. `ExecutionConfig.compaction` in runtime-types.ts adds `compactAtTokens?: number`. The shared schema from US-005 already accepts execution.compaction.compactAtTokens with no default; do not install the chat default on that shared setting.

Value imports across modules go through barrels (`check:alias-internals`): `chatCompactAtTokens` and `idleCompactAfterMs` from `src/chat/index.ts`. Export `DEFAULT_CHAT_COMPACT_AT_TOKENS` and `DEFAULT_IDLE_COMPACT_AFTER_MINUTES` from `src/config/index.ts`. Preserve disabled execution compaction and configured percentages when spreading; chat's 0 overrides an execution cap, rather than falling back to it.

**Scope** — In: extending prerequisite chat schema/type, defaults/constants/config barrel, execution runtime type, new chat-compaction.ts resolver helpers/chat barrel and native open-chat-session option composition. Out: US-005 shared threshold/schema arithmetic; US-007 createIdleCompactor, hook, ChatApp prop and CLI propagation; US-001–US-004 display. Compaction for ACP chat agents, chat subagents, and `nax run` story sessions (they keep `execution.compaction`). This exclusion concerns chat-specific policy; explicit execution.compaction remains supported for native non-chat sessions.

**Interface** — verbatim TypeScript:
```typescript
// packages/nax/src/config/schemas-chat.ts
export const DEFAULT_CHAT_COMPACT_AT_TOKENS = 200_000;
export const DEFAULT_IDLE_COMPACT_AFTER_MINUTES = 55;

// packages/nax/src/chat/chat-compaction.ts
export function chatCompactAtTokens(config: NaxConfig): number;          // chat.compaction.compactAtTokens ?? DEFAULT_CHAT_COMPACT_AT_TOKENS
export function idleCompactAfterMs(config: NaxConfig): number;           // minutes ?? DEFAULT_IDLE_COMPACT_AFTER_MINUTES, times 60000
```

Seam: US-006 consumes compactAtTokens (US-005) through nativeBackend({ compaction }); its seam AC enters at openChatSession and observes the stubbed nativeBackend. Extend existing option tests, add config/resolver tests, and assert subagents keep execution.compaction. The existing open-chat-session compaction assertion uses objectContaining, so the added compactAtTokens does not break it.

userStories.title: Idle compact while a job runs
acceptanceCriteria: [unit] A compactor with delayMs 3300000 and state { idle: true, runningJobId: "run-1", contextTokens: 50_000, acp: false } calls onDue("55m idle while job run-1 runs") after fake time advances 3300000 ms.
[unit] A compactor receiving the same qualifying state again at 3000000 ms still fires at 3300000 ms (a requalifying update does not restart the timer).
[unit] A compactor that fired for run-1 never calls onDue again for run-1, across later idle periods.
[unit] A compactor that fired for run-1 calls onDue for run-2 after a qualifying idle period with runningJobId run-2.
[unit] A compactor armed for run-1 that receives a qualifying state for run-2 at 1000000 ms calls onDue for run-2 at 4300000 ms and never for run-1.
[unit] A compactor with state { idle: true, contextTokens: 50_000, acp: false } and no runningJobId never calls onDue.
[unit] A compactor with acp true never calls onDue.
[unit] A compactor with contextTokens 19999 never calls onDue.
[unit] A compactor with contextTokens undefined never calls onDue.
[unit] A compactor with delayMs 0 never calls onDue.
[unit] A compactor whose state changes to idle false before delayMs elapses never calls onDue for that period.
[unit] dispose() on an armed compactor prevents onDue when fake time passes delayMs.

[integration] useIdleCompact with a host on a native model, turnRunning false, a running job and contextTokens 50000 calls note with 'idle compact: 55m idle while job <id> runs' and then calls compact once after delayMs 3300000.
[integration] useIdleCompact with a host whose current().model is acp:codex does not call compact after delayMs.

[integration] ChatApp rendered with idleCompactAfterMs 3300000, a fake host on a native model with a running job, and a finished turn whose context is 50000 tokens, shows an 'idle compact:' notice and calls host.compact once after fake time advances 3300000 ms.
[integration] The chat command with a loaded config whose chat.compaction.idleCompactAfterMinutes is 30 calls the injected deps.renderChat with props whose idleCompactAfterMs is 1800000.
[integration] When idle compaction fails for a running job, ChatApp shows compactTurn's error row and does not call host.compact again for that job across later qualifying idle periods.

[integration] ChatApp rendered without idleCompactAfterMs does not invoke host.compact after 3300000 ms of fake time with an idle native chat, a running job and contextTokens 50000, preserving the existing behavior of direct renders that do not opt into idle compaction.

routing.reasoning: Adds a once-per-job timer state machine and React/CLI/native-session integration with stale-closure, cancellation, busy-slot and failure/no-retry risks; strict session/token TDD override applies.

suggestedCriteria: When note and compact callbacks are replaced by a rerender before the armed timer fires, useIdleCompact invokes only the latest callbacks.
When a native chat changes to an acp: model while its idle timer is armed, passing the delay does not invoke compact.
When a running job disappears before the idle delay elapses, the compactor does not call onDue.
When contextTokens is exactly 20000 and all other conditions qualify, the compactor calls onDue after the delay.
When useIdleCompact unmounts with an armed timer, passing the delay invokes neither note nor compact.

analysis:
Goal and delivery: close #2942, #2943 and #2944 (part of #2946) by adding display-only live job panels, local turn-end clocks and native-chat-specific compaction defaults and idle compaction. This is an enhancement to the existing Bun/TypeScript React/Ink chat and the Node-compatible nax-agent library, not a new application. Preserve exactly US-001 through US-007 and their specified workdirs/dependencies. US-001 -> US-002 -> US-003 supplies the display path; US-004 is independent; US-005 -> US-006 -> US-007 supplies compaction. No version bumps or release work is required.

Discovery and prerequisite: codebase-memory MCP was unavailable in this tool set, so discovery used direct Read, Glob and Grep. Source citations below refer to this worktree, not presumed future files. The spec requires chat-workflow-flow to merge first. Currently packages/nax/src/config/schemas-chat.ts and runtime-types-chat.ts do not exist (confirmed direct lookup and config glob); NaxConfigSchema currently composes other schemas in packages/nax/src/config/schemas.ts:8-64 and :95 onward. US-006 must extend the prerequisite's ChatConfigSchema and ChatConfig after that merge, not invent a parallel chat block or silently implement the unrelated workflow feature. The second-pass context alignment retains those two spec-recommended paths in US-006 contextFiles as external-prerequisite context: they are not readable in this checkout yet, but must exist after chat-workflow-flow merges and before this feature executes. They are not files this story creates and must not be put in expectedFiles. Do not execute US-006 on this unprepared checkout; merge/rebase the prerequisite first, then revalidate both paths. Preserve the binding dependency arrays rather than adding a fictitious story.

Repository constraints: docs/architecture/ARCHITECTURE.md:13-39 indexes conventions, DI and testing; :160-180 documents hard/soft file limits, function limits, permission SSOT and cancellation rules. The spec explicitly freezes packages/nax/src/tui/chat/chat-status.ts at its source limit and permits only minimal hook calls/imports/props and the turn-end append adjustment in ChatApp.tsx; put substantive new logic in the named new modules. No setInterval. Every cancellable setTimeout/clearTimeout site needs the one-line documented mid-flight cancellation exception. Cross-module runtime values use barrels: advisor/index.ts exports decisionBody, chat/jobs/index.ts and chat/index.ts export panel API/types, chat/index.ts exports compaction API, config/index.ts exports chat defaults. TUI values come from @/chat and @/advisor, not alias-internal leaves. Source reads/spawns/timers need injectable seams; do not monkey-patch globals. nax-agent source is Node-compatible and must use #src/ imports or explicit .ts relative imports, never Bun APIs or nax imports. MIN_COMPACT_AT_TOKENS belongs on @nathapp/nax-agent/internal, never a new private import across the package boundary. A changed public facade declaration can affect api/nax-agent.api.txt; follow the existing API snapshot workflow when required, without exposing underscore seams on the public root.

US-001 existing model and sources: packages/nax/src/chat/jobs/job-types.ts:1-33 defines plan/run/finish/bot_review/bot_fix, the five states, pid/cwd/timestamps and optional cached cost/progress; :41-44 makes isRunJobKind include both run and finish. packages/nax/src/chat/jobs/job-runner.ts:33-61 exposes list (newest first), running, get, logTail, onChange and disposal. Keep that lifecycle read-only. packages/nax/src/chat/jobs/job-outcome.ts:23-43 already has _jobOutcomeDeps, projectProgress and private matchingStatus; the PID equality at :35 is essential to avoid showing another run's status. Expose readJobStatus over that read and preserve readRunProgress/resolveJobOutcome semantics (:39-43, :80-94). Reuse it, do not duplicate rendering. The ledger also has a trusted-decision action path (:93-121); this feature explicitly reads readDecisions for a display-only surface, never feeds that content to model context or action/approval resolution. Each source must fail independently to null/[]/empty text; one rejection must not discard successful sibling sources.
